Class ChildDispatch

java.lang.Object
com.trevlar.menukit.api.element.ChildDispatch
public final class ChildDispatch extends Object
The one way a list of elements is rendered and receives input (§0066). A panel's host dispatches to the panel's elements through it, and every element that contains others (ScrollContainer, Flow, Section, Tabs) dispatches to its children through it, so the order below is the same at every level.

The order

  1. Render: every shown child's render (render(List, RenderContext)), and in a second pass every shown child's renderOverlay (renderOverlay(List, RenderContext)), so an open popover is on top of every sibling whatever the declaration order. A host runs both passes; a container runs the base pass from its render and forwards the overlay pass from its own renderOverlay, so the host's second pass reaches its children after every base render.
  2. Click and wheel: a child whose open overlay (a Dropdown popover) contains the point gets the event exclusively. Otherwise the first child whose hit test contains the point and that consumes it.
  3. Release: every shown child, not hit-tested, so a drag ends wherever the cursor is.
  4. Key: each shown child in order until one consumes it.
  5. Outside click: every shown child, each deciding for itself.

Disabled

In a disabled context (the InputContext's flag: a disabled panel, or a container whose own disabledWhen holds) clicks, wheel and keys are not delivered at all. Releases and outside clicks are, so a drag or an open popover can still end.

Each child receives the context it was given: a container moves the origin to where it positions its children (InputContext.at(int, int)) before calling these, and adds its own disabled state (InputContext.disabledIf(boolean)). "Shown" is the child's own PanelElement.isVisible(); a host passes only the elements the window engine also shows.
